To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

electrophoresis of DNA and RNA provides an accurate assessment of the molecular quality and stability of stored human tissues and that the molecular quality of lung tissue is stable for up to 4 hours after excision.
electrophoretic analysis is a rapid and reliable means of assessing the molecular quality of banked human tissue.

electrophoresis procedures are a valuable measure of the quality of DNA and RNA extracted from human tissues and that DNA and RNA degradation in lung tissue is stable for up to 4-5 hours after excising.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a rapid and reliable method for assessing the molecular quality of banked human tissues.
the quality control of stored human tissues for molecular analyses, including PCR and RT-PCR.

the development of quality control procedures to determine the usefulness of stored human tissues for molecular analysis and to determine the stability of nucleic acids in human tissues after excision and storage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quality of human tissues for molecular studies is good and that the quality of DNA and RNA can be assessed by simple electrophoresis procedures.
the molecular quality of the tissue is not affected by storage time and that the molecular quality is dependent on the type of tissue and the storage conditions.
the majority of the tissues are suitable for molecular studies, but a significant number of the tissues are not suitable for certain molecular analyses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
80% of human tissues stored in liquid nitrogen have good-quality DNA, 60% have good-quality RNA, and the molecular quality of the tissues is stable for 5 hours after removal from the body.
the molecular quality of the human tissue specimens stored in the Cooperative Human Tissues Network, National Cancer Institutes, is generally good.

the majority of tissues stored at -70 degrees C are of good quality for further molecular analysis, and the electrophoresis procedures are the best method to determine the molecular quality of the tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular quality of tissues is dependent upon the type of tissue, the time of storage and, in some cases, the storage temperature.
electrophoresis is the most useful procedure for evaluating molecular quality of banked human tissues.
electrophoresis is an effective method to determine molecular quality in stored human tissues.
